Commentary.Commentary: ... THE RUN CHASE ...

New Zealand batters started on a brisk note but lost their momentum soon after Conway fell. Glenn Phillips played a good knock of 41 runs but fell for a slower ball. They kept on losing wickets whenever a good partnership was brewing for them. They ended up with 139 runs on the board and will be hoping for their bowlers to defend this one. Can they do it? Or will England continue to dominate? To find out, do join us in a bit for the second essay...

Winning the toss and choosing to bowl first turned out to be the perfect decision for the hosts. It was an all-round bowling performance from the English bowlers. They never let the Kiwi batters settle and kept on picking wickets at regular intervals. Luke Wood conceded three biggies in his very first over but made a fine comeback and chipped in three wickets. Brydon Carse picked up three wickets as well for his side. Adil Rashid, Moeen Ali, and Liam Livingstone picked up one wicket each whilst Sam Curran remained wicketless. They will certainly be the happier side going into the break.
